title: Source tax tariff: children
purpose: Ask the per-child questions, judged on the first working day, and derive each child's result and the child digit, including when a child makes the tariff H.

stories.title: Ask about children only of employees who need a source tax tariff
stories.i_want: to be asked whether I have children only when Lonio needs a source tax tariff code for me
stories.so_that: I do not give family details that no receiving party needs, while the source tax side still gets the child part of my tariff code
stories.priority_reason: The child digit is part of every tariff code Lonio computes (D-001); without it no tariff can be set. Asking employees who are not subject to source tax would break data minimisation (G-01, F-hr_transcript-b84498).

acceptance_criteria.title: Asked when a tariff code is needed
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is subject to source tax and a tariff code is needed for them (everyone subject to source tax, except Liechtenstein residents who return daily or expect at most 45 non-return days)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks whether the employee has biological or adopted children, answered yes or no; an answer is required. The answer is recorded for HR and used for the source tax tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Not asked when the employee is not subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland and is not subject to source tax (Swiss, holds a C permit, or married to / in a registered partnership with a Swiss national or C permit holder living in Switzerland)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee completes the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio does not ask about children and none of the child questions appear.

acceptance_criteria.title: Not asked of Liechtenstein residents in principle without source tax liability
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Liechtenstein and expects to return there daily, or does not return daily but expects at most 45 non-return days in the year
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee completes the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio does not ask about children, because no tariff code is computed; the result is 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement'. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: the Liechtenstein questions come before the children questions and skip them (D-040).

acceptance_criteria.title: Which children are meant depends on civil status
acceptance_criteria.given: the question about children is asked
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee is married or in a registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.then: the question covers biological or adopted children of the employee or of their spouse or registered partner; for single, divorced, separated or widowed employees it covers the employee's own biological or adopted children. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: registered partnership counts as married and separated as single, as in the calculator (D-003).

acceptance_criteria.title: No children means no child questions and child digit 0
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked about children
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers no
acceptance_criteria.then: no per-child questions are asked and the child digit of the tariff code is 0.

examples.name: Germany, single, no children

stories.title: One block per child: age status and household
stories.i_want: Lonio to ask, for each child, whether the child is a minor, an adult in first education or neither, and whether the child lives in the employee's household
stories.so_that: every child is judged the way the Zurich calculator judges it and children who cannot count are dropped without further questions
stories.priority_reason: These answers open or close every further child question and decide whether a child can count in the tariff code (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: One block of questions per child, no maximum
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered yes to having children
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee enters their children
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks the child questions once per child, in a separate block for each child; the employee can add as many children as they have and remove a child entered by mistake. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: there is no maximum number of children (D-044).

acceptance_criteria.title: Age status of each child, judged on the first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered yes to having children
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee fills in a child block
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks whether the child is 'Minor', 'Adult in first education' or 'Neither'; an answer is required. The employee answers as things stand on their first working day. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: a child's age is judged on the first working day (D-044).

acceptance_criteria.title: A child who is neither does not count and ends the block
acceptance_criteria.given: a child is neither a minor nor an adult in first education
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers 'Neither'
acceptance_criteria.then: no further questions are asked for this child and the child does not count towards the tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Household question for minors and adults in first education
acceptance_criteria.given: a child is a minor or an adult in first education
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee fills in that child's block
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks whether the child lives in the employee's household, answered yes or no; an answer is required. The answer decides which further questions follow for this child.

stories.title: Minor child living in the employee's household
stories.i_want: Lonio to ask about custody, a common household with the other parent, alternating custody and the main financial contributor for a minor child living in the employee's household, and to derive whether the child counts
stories.so_that: the child digit and a possible tariff H match what the Zurich calculator gives for this child
stories.priority_reason: Minor children in the household are the most common child case; a wrong result gives a wrong tariff code, which Lonio now computes instead of HR (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Custody asked for a minor child in the household
acceptance_criteria.given: a child is a minor and lives in the employee's household
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee fills in that child's block
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks whether parental custody is 'Shared custody' or 'Sole custody'; an answer is required. This applies whatever the employee's civil status.

examples.name: Single, minor in household

acceptance_criteria.title: Sole custody: the child counts
acceptance_criteria.given: a minor child lives in the employee's household and the employee has sole custody
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the child's result
acceptance_criteria.then: no further questions are asked for this child; the child counts, and for a single, divorced, separated or widowed employee it counts with H (makes the tariff H). Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: registered partnership is treated as married and separated as single (D-003).

acceptance_criteria.title: Shared custody and common household with the other parent
acceptance_criteria.given: a minor child lives in the employee's household with shared custody
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee states whether they live in a common household with the child's other parent (yes or no, required)
acceptance_criteria.then: if yes and the employee is married or in a registered partnership, the child counts and no further question is asked; if yes and the employee is single, divorced, separated or widowed, Lonio asks who makes the larger financial contribution ('The employee' or 'The other parent'): the employee gives 'counts with H', the other parent gives 'does not count'. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: the single case with the employee as main contributor is inferred and is checked against the calculator before go-live (D-046, D-009; see OQ-calculator-coverage).

acceptance_criteria.title: Shared custody without common household: alternating custody
acceptance_criteria.given: a minor child lives in the employee's household with shared custody and the employee does not live in a common household with the other parent
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee states whether there is alternating custody (yes or no, required)
acceptance_criteria.then: without alternating custody the child does not count for a married employee or registered partner and counts with H for a single, divorced, separated or widowed employee. With alternating custody Lonio asks who makes the larger financial contribution: if the employee, the child counts (married or registered partnership) or counts with H (single, divorced, separated, widowed); if the other parent, the child does not count. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: observed calculator rows win; the married case with the employee as main contributor and the single case with the other parent as main contributor are inferred and checked before go-live (D-046, D-009; see OQ-calculator-coverage).

stories.title: Minor child not living in the employee's household
stories.i_want: Lonio to ask about shared custody (married employees and registered partners) or parental care (single, divorced, separated or widowed employees), alternating custody and the main financial contributor for a minor child living elsewhere, and to derive whether the child counts
stories.so_that: a child living elsewhere only counts in the tariff code when the calculator would count it
stories.priority_reason: A wrong per-child result gives a wrong tariff code, which Lonio now computes instead of HR (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Shared custody or parental care, depending on civil status
acceptance_criteria.given: a child is a minor and does not live in the employee's household
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee fills in that child's block
acceptance_criteria.then: a married employee or registered partner is asked whether custody is shared (yes or no); a single, divorced, separated or widowed employee is asked whether they have parental care (yes or no). The answer is required. The custody question for children in the household is not asked. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: registered partnership is treated as married and separated as single (D-003).

acceptance_criteria.title: No shared custody or parental care: the child does not count
acceptance_criteria.given: a minor child does not live in the employee's household
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers no to shared custody or to parental care
acceptance_criteria.then: no further questions are asked for this child and the child does not count.

acceptance_criteria.title: Alternating custody and main financial contributor
acceptance_criteria.given: a minor child does not live in the employee's household and the employee has shared custody or parental care
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee states whether there is alternating custody (yes or no, required) and, with alternating custody, who makes the larger financial contribution ('The employee' or 'The other parent', required)
acceptance_criteria.then: the child counts only with alternating custody and the employee as main contributor: it counts for a married employee or registered partner and counts with H for a single, divorced, separated or widowed employee. Without alternating custody, or with the other parent as main contributor, the child does not count. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: the two 'does not count' cases are inferred and checked against the calculator before go-live (D-046, D-009; see OQ-calculator-coverage).

stories.title: Adult child in first education
stories.i_want: Lonio to ask, for an adult child in first education, about a common household with the other parent, the main financial contributor and whether the employee provides more than 50% of the child's maintenance, and to derive whether the child counts
stories.so_that: adult children in first education count in the tariff code exactly when the calculator counts them
stories.priority_reason: A wrong per-child result gives a wrong tariff code, which Lonio now computes instead of HR (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Adult child in the household: common household with the other parent
acceptance_criteria.given: a child is an adult in first education and lives in the employee's household
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee fills in that child's block
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks whether the employee lives in a common household with the child's other parent (yes or no, required). Custody, shared custody, parental care and alternating custody are not asked for adult children.

acceptance_criteria.title: Common household with the other parent
acceptance_criteria.given: an adult child in first education lives in the employee's household and the employee lives in a common household with the other parent
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the child's result
acceptance_criteria.then: for a married employee or registered partner the child counts and no further question is asked; a single, divorced, separated or widowed employee is asked who makes the larger financial contribution: the employee gives 'counts with H', the other parent gives 'does not count'. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: both single cases are inferred and checked against the calculator before go-live (D-046, D-009; see OQ-calculator-coverage).

acceptance_criteria.title: In the household without common household: more than 50% of maintenance
acceptance_criteria.given: an adult child in first education lives in the employee's household and the employee does not live in a common household with the other parent
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee states whether they mainly (more than 50%) provide for the child's maintenance (yes or no, required)
acceptance_criteria.then: with yes the child counts for a married employee or registered partner and counts with H for a single, divorced, separated or widowed employee; with no the child does not count. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: the married 'counts' case and the 'does not count' case are inferred and checked before go-live (D-046, D-009; see OQ-calculator-coverage).

acceptance_criteria.given: an adult child in first education does not live in the employee's household

stories.title: Child digit of the tariff code and go-live check of the child paths
stories.i_want: Lonio to turn the per-child results into the child digit of the tariff code and to signal when a child makes the tariff H
stories.so_that: I no longer click through the Zurich calculator for each child, and the computed tariff code is trusted only after the unexplored child paths have been checked
stories.priority_reason: HR's manual calculator step is replaced by the computed tariff code (D-001); a wrong digit means wrong source tax deductions, so the go-live check is a release condition (D-009).

acceptance_criteria.title: Child digit is the number of counted children
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee needs a tariff code
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the child digit
acceptance_criteria.then: each child whose result is 'counts' or 'counts with H' adds 1 and each child whose result is 'does not count' adds 0; the child digit is the total over all children (for example three counted children give C3Y for a married employee whose spouse works), and 0 if the employee has no children. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: there is no maximum number of children (D-044); more than 3 children is part of the go-live check (D-009).

examples.name: Child that counts adds 1
Child counted with H adds 1
Child that does not count adds 0
No children gives 0

acceptance_criteria.title: A child counted with H makes the tariff H
acceptance_criteria.given: a single, divorced, separated or widowed employee has at least one child whose result is 'counts with H'
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the tariff code
acceptance_criteria.then: the tariff letter is H and the child digit still counts every counted child (for example one child that counts and one that counts with H give H2). Married employees and registered partners never get 'counts with H'. The tariff letter itself is set by the tariff letter rule of the source tax tariff section.

acceptance_criteria.title: Observed calculator rows win; inferred rows are checked before go-live
acceptance_criteria.given: a per-child result that rests on a case not observed in the calculator (marked inferred in the per-child stories), more than 3 children, or a combination of child, residence, denomination and civil status not explored
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio is prepared for go-live
acceptance_criteria.then: a domain expert compares Lonio's computed tariff code with the Zurich calculator for these cases before release; where an observed calculator result exists it decides the per-child result. This is a non-blocking go-live condition (see OQ-calculator-coverage). Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert (D-046).

acceptance_criteria.title: Results follow the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: the questionnaire has been submitted and a child answer is later changed by HR (for example a new child)
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the per-child results and the child digit
acceptance_criteria.then: they are always derived again from the latest answers; the per-child results and the child digit are recorded for HR as part of the tariff code.
